question: Have the owner (a human, not an agent: the PDFs are behind HubSpot forms) obtain the Chariot/K2D DAF Fundraising Report 2024, 2025 and 2026 PDFs and the M+R Benchmarks 2026 PDF (mrbenchmarks.com blocks Claude agents in robots.txt). Then extract: the DAF-gift identification method, the major-gift threshold behind '>22% of major-gift revenue', year-by-year mean and median DAF gift and DAF gift counts 2021-2025, sector and size exhibits, the participant list, and M+R's 2025 DAF-per-online-dollar by sector
conclusion_affected: direction-nonprofit-daf-benchmarks.md §0/§3 (several values are [R]/[S]; sector and size cuts incomplete); DAF-INDUSTRY-REPORT nonprofit-side economics
rationale: The only nonprofit-file DAF series is vendor-run and its definitions are gated; NPB007-009 and NPB031 rest on unfetched snippets, one of which conflicts with the published 23x ratio

question: Build an independent, non-vendor estimate of DAF share of recipient revenue. Sum the repo's whitelisted-sponsor Schedule I grant lines (FY2023-FY2024, netted of DAF-to-DAF) by recipient EIN, and divide by each recipient's Form 990 Part VIII line 1h (total contributions). Report the distribution (median, P25/P75, pooled) by NTEE sector and revenue band, excluding universities, hospitals, foundations and DAF sponsors, and compare with Chariot's 12-13% and sector 4-24%
conclusion_affected: Plausibility of the ~10-13% DAF share; size and sector variation (currently only vendor cuts); TAM for nonprofit-side DAF products
rationale: No public benchmark gives a size or sector cut from non-vendor data, and Form 990 does not separate DAF receipts. The repo already caches Schedule I lines and recipient sectors, so a recipient-level share is computable. Coverage is a floor: Schedule I itemises grants over $5,000 only

question: Reconcile nonprofit-side DAF growth with sponsor-side grant growth for CY2025. Assemble FY2025/CY2025 grant totals and grant counts from the large national sponsors' published reports and FY2025 990s, and compare with M+R's +44% DAF revenue / +23% gifts and Chariot's 2025 medians. Test whether the 2025 surge is concentrated in mass-market (<$1,000) DAF gifts
conclusion_affected: Trend statements for 2025 in direction-nonprofit-daf-benchmarks.md §3.5; FY2025 extension of netted market totals
rationale: The repo's netted totals stop at FY2024, while the nonprofit-side 2025 surge (+44%) is unverified against sponsor data. The gap between M+R's 2024 +6% and netted FY2024 +15% also needs explaining
